item.title: Main :: Aion 2 Crafting Strategies: Choosing Safety or Risk with our team
item.description:
Author: JackWalker
Subject: Aion 2 Crafting Strategies: Choosing Safety or Risk with our team
Posted: Thu Nov 05, 2026 7:49 am (GMT 0)

Crafting is one of the more interesting parts of endgame progression in Aion 2. Once players start working toward powerful weapons and armor, every crafting attempt becomes a decision about resources, time, and risk. Materials can take considerable effort to collect, and losing them because of an unsuccessful attempt is never pleasant. This is especially important when you are also trying to manage your Aion 2 Kinah and save enough resources for other upgrades.

The introduction of the Guaranteed Success recipe gives players another way to approach equipment crafting. Instead of relying entirely on random results, you can secure a base-level item without worrying about the normal failure chance. However, this convenience comes with a trade-off: you lose access to Great Success and the possibility of crafting a higher-tier Splendent item. Understanding these differences can help you avoid spending materials on a method that does not match your goals.
Two Crafting Methods With Different Goals
Guaranteed Success and standard crafting are designed for different types of players.

The Guaranteed Success recipe provides a 100% success rate. Once you have the required materials, you receive the base-level equipment. There is no chance of losing those materials through a failed craft, but the recipe cannot activate the Combo or Great Success mechanic.

Standard crafting offers more potential but also introduces additional uncertainty. Its success rate depends on your crafting proficiency and generally ranges from approximately 74% to the mid-90s%. Even if the initial attempt succeeds, you still need to pass additional random checks to obtain the upgraded result.
Feature Guaranteed Success Standard Crafting
Success rate 100% Around 74% to mid-90s%
Great Success Disabled Available
Splendent result Not available Possible
Material risk No failure loss Materials can be lost
Item status Character-bound Can remain tradeable
Main purpose Reliable upgrades Higher-tier crafting

For players who simply need better equipment, the guaranteed recipe is often easier to plan around. Those looking for rare results will probably prefer the standard method.
Why Great Success Requires More Than Luck
The standard crafting process involves several stages, which explains why getting a Splendent item is not as easy as seeing a successful crafting message.

First, the initial crafting attempt must succeed. Your proficiency influences the success rate, but it does not eliminate the possibility of failure.

Next, the Great Success or Combo activation needs to occur. The activation chance is approximately 25%, giving players an opportunity to produce an upgraded version instead of the regular item.

Finally, the upgraded crafting attempt must also succeed. This additional check means that activating Great Success does not automatically guarantee the highest-tier equipment.

According to the supplied probability estimates, the overall chance of obtaining a Splendent result from one standard attempt is approximately 21% to 23%.

This distinction matters when planning your materials. A 25% Combo chance is not the same as a 25% chance of receiving the finished upgraded item. Players should consider the entire crafting process rather than focusing on one individual probability.
When Guaranteed Success Makes More Sense
For most players working with limited resources, Guaranteed Success is a sensible starting point.

Imagine that you have finally collected enough materials for an important weapon upgrade. Your current equipment is slowing down your progression, and you would rather improve your character immediately than risk losing everything. In this situation, the guaranteed recipe offers a straightforward solution.

The same logic applies to armor pieces that you intend to equip permanently. Since the finished item becomes character-bound, you should only choose this method when you are comfortable keeping the equipment.

It is also useful for players who prefer predictable progression. You can plan your crafting materials around a known result instead of repeatedly attempting the same recipe and hoping for a better outcome.
When Standard Crafting Is Worth Trying
Standard crafting becomes more attractive when your target is a Splendent weapon or another high-tier equipment piece.

It is also the better option if you want to produce equipment for the marketplace. Unlike the guaranteed recipe, successful standard crafts can remain unbound, allowing eligible items to be traded.

However, crafting for profit requires more planning than simply hoping for a rare result. You need to consider material costs, possible failed attempts, marketplace demand, and the price players are willing to pay.

Having additional resources available makes this approach more comfortable because one unsuccessful attempt will not completely stop your progression.
A Practical Way to Manage Your Crafting Budget
A balanced strategy is to separate essential upgrades from optional crafting projects. Use Guaranteed Success when you need a dependable equipment improvement, and reserve standard crafting for situations where the potential reward justifies the risk.

Players who need to replenish their currency before another crafting session may also compare different options for obtaining cheap Aion 2 Kinah, while keeping their spending within a reasonable budget.
Final Thoughts on Choosing the Right Recipe
Neither method is automatically the best choice. Guaranteed Success protects your materials and gives you dependable equipment, while standard crafting offers a chance to reach higher tiers and produce tradeable results. The better option depends on your equipment goals, proficiency, and willingness to accept losses. Before starting an expensive recipe, decide whether you need a reliable upgrade or are genuinely prepared to gamble for something better.

item.title: Main :: MSCW Arrow Crafting Guide: Save Mesos with our team
item.description:
Author: JackWalker
Subject: MSCW Arrow Crafting Guide: Save Mesos with our team
Posted: Thu Nov 05, 2026 7:48 am (GMT 0)

Arrow crafting is a useful feature in MapleStory Classic World, especially for players who have chosen the Bowman or Crossbowman job. Ammunition is something you need throughout your leveling journey, and constantly buying it from NPC shops can become an unnecessary expense. While MapleStory Classic World Items are important for character progression, keeping enough arrows in your inventory is just as important when you spend hours fighting monsters.

Fortunately, you don't need to depend entirely on merchants. The Woodcrafting profession allows you to turn common monster drops into large batches of arrows. The process is straightforward, the required materials are relatively easy to collect, and the savings can add up over time. Here is how to get started and make the most of this profession.
Where to Learn Woodcrafting
Before making arrows, you need access to Woodcrafting. The profession is managed by Vicious, an NPC trainer located in Henesys. Visit him to get started and unlock the basic crafting recipes.

One advantage of arrow crafting is that you don't need to spend much time leveling the profession before making useful ammunition. The basic recipes are available at Woodcrafting Level 1, so even newer characters can benefit from them.

Processed Wood is the main material required for arrow production. You can obtain it through two different recipes, depending on your profession level and available resources.
Processed Wood and Arrow Recipes
There are two ways to produce Processed Wood. The first uses Tree Branches, while the second requires Firewood. Both methods produce one Processed Wood, but their costs and EXP rewards are different.
Recipe Required Level Materials Meso Cost Result
Processed Wood 1 10 Tree Branches 100 1 Processed Wood
Processed Wood 2 5 Firewood 200 1 Processed Wood
Bow Arrows 1 1 Processed Wood + 1 Stiff Feather 0 500 Arrows
Crossbow Arrows 1 1 Processed Wood + 1 Stiff Feather 0 500 Arrows

For most players, the Tree Branch recipe is the better option when the goal is saving money. It costs only 100 Mesos and requires materials that can be collected during normal monster hunting.

The Firewood recipe costs twice as much, but it provides twice the Woodcrafting EXP. This makes it worth considering if you are trying to develop the profession rather than simply produce ammunition.

Once you have one Processed Wood and one Stiff Feather, you can choose the arrow recipe that matches your weapon. Each crafting attempt produces 500 arrows, which is a convenient amount for extended training sessions.
How Arrow Conversion Works
Another useful feature is the ability to exchange Bow Arrows for Crossbow Arrows, or the other way around.

For example, if you are playing a Crossbowman but have collected Bow Arrows from monster drops, you don't necessarily need to leave them unused. You can visit the crafting table and convert them into the ammunition your character needs.

The exchange rate is 2-to-1. Every 10 arrows of one type become five arrows of the other type.

There is no Meso fee for this conversion, but it does not provide Woodcrafting EXP. Since you lose half the original ammunition, it is better to collect the correct arrow type whenever possible.
How Much Can You Save?
Basic arrows are sold by NPC general stores for 1 Meso each. Buying 500 arrows therefore costs 500 Mesos.

Crafting offers a cheaper alternative if you collect the materials yourself.
Method Cost for 500 Arrows
NPC Shop 500 Mesos
Tree Branch Recipe 100 Mesos
Firewood Recipe 200 Mesos

Using Tree Branches saves 400 Mesos per batch, while the Firewood method saves 300 Mesos.

These figures assume you farm the materials instead of purchasing them from other players. If you need to buy Tree Branches, Firewood, or Stiff Feathers, remember to include those expenses when comparing the two methods.

For Archers who regularly consume ammunition, these savings can make a noticeable difference over multiple training sessions.
Can You Make Money Selling Arrows?
Although arrow crafting is useful, it is not a reliable way to earn Mesos. The problem is that basic arrows are already extremely cheap at NPC shops.

Most players have little reason to purchase crafted arrows from another player when they can simply visit a merchant. The materials are also relatively accessible, so there is little room to charge a competitive price.

Woodcrafting EXP is another limitation. Basic ammunition recipes are convenient, but they are not necessarily the most efficient way to reach higher profession levels. More advanced weapons require different recipes and potentially more expensive materials.

Players who want to explore the wider equipment economy should treat crafting as a way to support their characters rather than an automatic source of income.
Final Thoughts on Arrow Crafting
For Bowman and Crossbowman players, Woodcrafting is worth learning because it helps reduce one of the recurring expenses of leveling. You can gather materials while exploring, prepare ammunition in batches, and avoid returning to NPC shops every time your supply runs low.

Managing your character's overall economy also means understanding which expenses are worth reducing and which activities are better suited to earning currency. When planning your progression, MapleStory Global Mesos can be part of the wider discussion about managing equipment purchases and other character expenses.

The best approach is simple: use Woodcrafting to supply your own arrows, choose the Tree Branch recipe when saving money is your priority, and leave higher-level crafting for when you have a specific equipment goal.

item.title: Main :: WoW Forever Leveling Routes: Tips for Levels 30–45
item.description:
Author: JackWalker
Subject: WoW Forever Leveling Routes: Tips for Levels 30–45
Posted: Thu Nov 05, 2026 7:46 am (GMT 0)

Reaching level 30 in WoW Forever is where leveling starts to become more interesting. The early zones are mostly behind you, enemies are getting stronger, and choosing the wrong questing area can waste a surprising amount of time. Managing your WoW Forever Gold also becomes more important because you will soon need to pay for better training, equipment, repairs, and your first mount. Having a clear route makes this part of the journey much easier.

For players who want to reach level 45 without spending hours wandering between zones, the best approach is to combine familiar Classic areas with the new Riverglades content. WoW Forever Gold should be managed carefully during this stage, especially if you are still saving for level 40 riding training. Instead of completing every available quest, focus on objectives that match your character's level and can be finished during the same trip.
Levels 30–35: Finish Your Existing Quest Hubs
At level 30, there is no immediate reason to abandon every familiar zone. Several areas still provide useful experience, particularly if you have unfinished quest chains.

Northern Stranglethorn Vale is a good starting point for both factions. Nesingwary's Expedition offers hunting quests that send players after different creatures throughout the jungle. These objectives can be combined, allowing you to complete several quests without constantly returning to the camp.

Arathi Highlands is another reliable option. Alliance players can use Refuge Pointe as their main hub, while Horde players should visit Hammerfall. Both factions have opportunities to complete quests suitable for characters around this level.

Horde players can also consider Desolace and Thousand Needles. Freewind Post is a useful location for picking up additional quests in Thousand Needles. These alternatives become particularly helpful when popular quest areas are crowded.

The main goal is to reach level 35 without spending too much time fighting enemies that are significantly stronger than your character.
Levels 35–40: Make Riverglades Your Priority
Riverglades is one of the biggest additions to the mid-level experience in WoW Forever. With more than 150 new quests designed for the level 35–45 bracket, it gives players another substantial source of experience instead of relying entirely on traditional Classic zones.

Once you arrive, visit the available quest hubs and collect nearby objectives before heading into the surrounding areas. Pay attention to quests that involve the same enemies or locations. Completing them together saves travel time and makes each trip more productive.

Alliance players can reach Riverglades through Eastern Kingdoms travel connections. Horde players have a specialized boat route from Tanaris to Powderfuse Port.

Do not rush through every area simply because the quests are available. WoW Forever does not use level scaling, so some enemies can still be dangerous if you enter an area too early. If a particular quest becomes difficult, move to another objective and return when your character is stronger.
Levels 40–43: Add Krol'dok Stronghold
Once you reach level 40, Krol'dok Stronghold becomes another option for your leveling schedule.

Dungeon quest experience is especially valuable in WoW Forever. Although monster experience inside dungeons is slightly lower, completing dungeon quests provides significantly boosted experience rewards.

Before joining a group, collect the available quests and check whether your party members have similar objectives. This makes it easier to complete several tasks in one run rather than repeating the dungeon unnecessarily.

Dungeon runs also provide opportunities to improve your equipment. Even if you prefer solo questing, completing an occasional group activity can help break up the routine.

Level 40 is also the time to think seriously about riding training. Your first mount makes traveling between quest objectives much faster, particularly in large areas such as Riverglades and Tanaris.
Levels 43–45: Move Toward Tanaris and Feralas
As you approach level 43, start looking at the traditional higher-level zones.

Tanaris is an excellent choice. Gadgetzan provides access to pirate-related quests and desert exploration objectives. Collect several quests before leaving town so that you can complete multiple tasks during one journey.

Dustwallow Marsh is another useful alternative. Alliance players can explore the Theramore area, while Horde players can follow their faction's available quest chains. If Tanaris is overcrowded, changing zones is often more efficient than waiting for quest objectives.

Feralas and The Hinterlands also become useful around levels 42–44. However, check the enemy levels before committing to a long questing session.
Managing Gold and Travel Time
Your leveling route is only one part of efficient progression. Gold management can make a noticeable difference, particularly when you reach level 40.

Avoid purchasing every minor skill upgrade immediately. Prioritize abilities that you regularly use, keep enough gold for repairs, and save for riding training. Before replacing equipment, compare the actual stats instead of assuming every new item is better.

A mount also changes how you should approach questing. You can cover more ground between objectives and spend less time running back to quest hubs. This becomes especially useful when moving between Riverglades, Tanaris, and other large zones.
Final Thoughts
The most practical route is to complete Stranglethorn Vale and Arathi Highlands around levels 30–35, spend the next several levels exploring Riverglades, and then transition into Krol'dok Stronghold, Tanaris, and other suitable zones. Players who need additional resources can also plan their progression and decide whether to buy WoW Forever Gold rather than spend unnecessary time farming. The important thing is to keep your character properly equipped and avoid wasting time in zones that no longer offer suitable challenges.

Want to spend less time farming and more time enjoying your leveling journey? offers a convenient way to explore WoW Forever Gold options and prepare for your next adventure. Whether you are saving for your level 40 mount, upgrading your equipment, or preparing for tougher dungeon runs, having enough gold can make progression more comfortable. Visit to check the available WoW Forever Gold options and find the resources you need for your journey.

item.title: Development :: RE: New programming language MasterBASIC
item.description:
Author: Materion
Posted: Thu Nov 05, 2026 6:35 am (GMT 0)

Update 1.5.0

https://github.com/MaterzokMateusz/MasterBASIC/releases/tag/Release1.5

MasterBASIC 1.5.0 can now load music from text files: each song or sound effect can live in its own .txt file. The Master System has no disk, so the files are read when you build the game and copied into the cartridge; the game can’t load new files while it runs.

MUSIC theme = "music/theme.txt" ' one song per text file
MUSIC fanfare = "music/fanfare.txt" ONCE ' a jingle that plays once
SFX boing = "music/boing.txt" ' one sound effect per text file
SOUND "music/more.pml" ' a file with many songs (can be used several times)

PLAYMUSIC theme
PLAYSFX boing
